"""Generate visualizations for the EU economic data storytelling report."""
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.rcParams.update({
    "figure.facecolor": "white",
    "axes.facecolor": "white",
    "font.size": 11,
    "axes.grid": True,
    "grid.alpha": 0.3,
    "axes.spines.top": False,
    "axes.spines.right": False,
})

df = pd.read_csv("eu_economic_data.csv")
countries = ["Germany", "France", "Italy", "Spain", "Netherlands", "Poland", "Sweden"]
eu = df[df.Country == "EU_Total"].set_index("Year")
cdf = df[df.Country.isin(countries)]
palette = {
    "Germany": "#1f3a5f", "France": "#385c8f", "Italy": "#2E86AB",
    "Spain": "#6fae5a", "Netherlands": "#f4a261", "Poland": "#e76f51",
    "Sweden": "#8a6fb0",
}

# Chart 1: EU headline story - inflation tamed, growth positive, jobs held
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(11, 7))
ax = axes[0, 0]
ax.plot(eu.index, eu["Inflation_Pct"], marker="o", lw=2.5, color="#e76f51")
ax.axhline(2.0, ls="--", color="gray", lw=1)
ax.text(2021.2, 2.1, "ECB 2% target", fontsize=9, color="gray")
for x, y in zip(eu.index, eu["Inflation_Pct"]):
    ax.annotate(f"{y:.1f}%", (x, y), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 9), ha="center")
ax.set_title("Inflation: 9.2% → 2.4% in two years", fontweight="bold")
ax.set_ylabel("HICP inflation (%)")
ax.set_xticks([2022, 2023, 2024])

ax = axes[0, 1]
ax.plot(eu.index, eu["Unemployment_Pct"], marker="o", lw=2.5, color="#2E86AB")
for x, y in zip(eu.index, eu["Unemployment_Pct"]):
    ax.annotate(f"{y:.1f}%", (x, y), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 9), ha="center")
ax.set_title("Unemployment: labor market held firm", fontweight="bold")
ax.set_ylabel("Unemployment rate (%)")
ax.set_xticks([2022, 2023, 2024])

ax = axes[1, 0]
ax.plot(eu.index, eu["GDP_Growth_Pct"], marker="o", lw=2.5, color="#385c8f")
ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=0.8)
for x, y in zip(eu.index, eu["GDP_Growth_Pct"]):
    ax.annotate(f"{y:+.1f}%", (x, y), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 9), ha="center")
ax.set_title("Real GDP growth: no recession", fontweight="bold")
ax.set_ylabel("Real GDP growth (%)")
ax.set_xticks([2022, 2023, 2024])

ax = axes[1, 1]
ax.plot(eu.index, eu["Public_Debt_Pct_GDP"], marker="o", lw=2.5, color="#6fae5a")
for x, y in zip(eu.index, eu["Public_Debt_Pct_GDP"]):
    ax.annotate(f"{y:.1f}%", (x, y), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 9), ha="center")
ax.set_title("Public debt: 84.0% → 80.1% of GDP", fontweight="bold")
ax.set_ylabel("Debt-to-GDP (%)")
ax.set_xticks([2022, 2023, 2024])

fig.suptitle("The EU 2022–2024: Taming inflation without breaking the economy", fontsize=14, fontweight="bold")
fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.96])
fig.savefig("charts/eu_headline.png", dpi=150)
plt.close(fig)

# Chart 2: GDP growth by country (grouped bars)
years = [2022, 2023, 2024]
x = range(len(countries))
w = 0.27
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 6))
for i, y in enumerate(years):
    vals = cdf[cdf.Year == y].set_index("Country").loc[countries, "GDP_Growth_Pct"]
    ax.bar([p + (i - 1) * w for p in x], vals, width=w, label=str(y), color=[palette[c] for c in countries], alpha=0.75 + 0.1 * i)
ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=0.8)
ax.axhline(0.9, color="#e76f51", ls="--", lw=1.2)
ax.text(6.6, 1.05, "EU 2024 avg. (+0.9%)", color="#e76f51", fontsize=9)
ax.set_xticks(list(x))
ax.set_xticklabels(countries)
ax.set_ylabel("Real GDP growth (%)")
ax.set_title("Divergence: Spain accelerates, Germany contracts", fontweight="bold")
ax.legend(title="Year", ncol=3, frameon=False)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("charts/growth_by_country.png", dpi=150)
plt.close(fig)

# Chart 3: Trade balance before/after (2022 vs 2024)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 6))
bal22 = cdf[cdf.Year == 2022].set_index("Country").loc[countries, "Trade_Balance_Billion_EUR"]
bal24 = cdf[cdf.Year == 2024].set_index("Country").loc[countries, "Trade_Balance_Billion_EUR"]
ypos = range(len(countries))[::-1]
ax.barh([p + 0.2 for p in ypos], bal22, height=0.4, label="2022", color="#d9d9d9")
ax.barh([p - 0.2 for p in ypos], bal24, height=0.4, label="2024", color="#2E86AB")
ax.axvline(0, color="black", lw=0.8)
for p, c in zip(ypos, countries):
    ax.text(bal24[c] + 3 if bal24[c] >= 0 else bal24[c] - 3, p - 0.2, f"{bal24[c]:+.0f}", va="center",
            ha="left" if bal24[c] >= 0 else "right", fontsize=9, color="#1a4a66", fontweight="bold")
ax.set_yticks(list(ypos))
ax.set_yticklabels(countries)
ax.set_xlabel("Trade balance (€ bn)")
ax.set_title("Trade rebalancing: EU deficit shrinks from −€198bn to −€8bn", fontweight="bold")
ax.legend(frameon=False)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("charts/trade_balance.png", dpi=150)
plt.close(fig)

# Chart 4: Debt-to-GDP paths by country
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 6))
for c in countries:
    s = cdf[cdf.Country == c].set_index("Year")["Public_Debt_Pct_GDP"]
    ax.plot(s.index, s, marker="o", lw=2, label=c, color=palette[c])
ax.plot(eu.index, eu["Public_Debt_Pct_GDP"], marker="D", lw=3, ls="--", color="black", label="EU total")
ax.set_ylabel("Public debt (% of GDP)")
ax.set_title("Fiscal paths diverge: Italy and Spain deleverage, France drifts up", fontweight="bold")
ax.set_xticks([2022, 2023, 2024])
ax.legend(frameon=False, ncol=4)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("charts/debt_paths.png", dpi=150)
plt.close(fig)

# Chart 5: Unemployment paths
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 6))
for c in countries:
    s = cdf[cdf.Country == c].set_index("Year")["Unemployment_Pct"]
    ax.plot(s.index, s, marker="o", lw=2, label=c, color=palette[c])
ax.plot(eu.index, eu["Unemployment_Pct"], marker="D", lw=3, ls="--", color="black", label="EU total")
ax.set_ylabel("Unemployment rate (%)")
ax.set_title("Jobs gap narrows: Spain improves, Sweden slips", fontweight="bold")
ax.set_xticks([2022, 2023, 2024])
ax.legend(frameon=False, ncol=4)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("charts/unemployment_paths.png", dpi=150)
plt.close(fig)

print("Charts written to ./charts")
